decision: SCORE lambda tuning probe 2026-09-17: four short SCORE cells on Qwen at 7 QPS x 2,000 requests, identical in every respect to the canonical qwen-score-7 cell of scripts/cloud/sfs-score-campaign-20260917.json except for the Lagrange multiplier lambda of the SCORE objective d_t = argmax_i Qhat_i - lambda (w_C c_i Shat_i + w_L W_i + w_L s_i Shat_i) and for the shortened budget. The SCORE paper (Lakha, Yu, Shahout, ICLR 2025 SLLM workshop) states that lambda is the knob that enforces the cost and latency constraints while w_C and w_L only set their relative importance, and never fixes its value; its scales (quality 1..5, outputs up to 512 tokens, 1 request/second, two models) differ from ours (quality in [0, 1], outputs up to 8192 tokens, 6-8.3 QPS, three models), so lambda is the single quantity swept here. w_C = w_L = 1 is kept and nothing else is tuned. Our SCORE baseline at lambda = 5e-4, the multiplier chosen for the SFS objective, collapses (TTFT SLO attainment 6.5 percent at 6 QPS and 3.8 percent at 7 QPS, median TTFT about 215 s), which is what this probe is meant to diagnose. NOT REPORTABLE: every cell carries data_role tuning_probe and a 2,000-request budget, its id is prefixed with probe- so it can never collide with a reportable cell id, and the worker writes the receipts to <state>/completed-probes, outside the canonical completed ledger. The lambda chosen from this probe must then be used for ALL SCORE cells (6/7/8/8.3 QPS), which are rerun in full at 16,000 requests under the SFS/SCORE overlay.

reference.note: The probes stand in for the canonical qwen-score-7 cell (same family, policy, rate, remaining-length rule and source lineage) at four multipliers; the lambda = 5e-4 probe is the control for the value the campaign overlay currently carries. These 2,000-request points are a tuning probe and are NOT reportable: they never replace qwen-score-7 or any other SCORE cell, are never collated into the canonical completed ledger, and only select the lambda under which the full 16,000-request SCORE cells are then rerun. A pool runs all four probes in one qualification and smokes once, at the bundle's own lambda.

worker.semantics: Each cell's lambda_weight replaces the bundle's --lambda-weight for that cell's router run only; the per-pool smoke keeps the bundle value. The router records it in point.json config.lambda_weight, and the worker refuses the cell unless the recorded value matches. qualification.json and every probe receipt carry lambda_weight, lambda_weights (the sweep's level list) and data_role tuning_probe.
worker.command: python -m scripts.cloud.worker campaign --bundle <bundle> --models <models.json> --state <state> --output <output> --family qwen --gpus <4 gpu ids> --campaign scripts/cloud/score-lambda-sweep-20260917.json --cells probe-qwen-score-7-lambda5em4,probe-qwen-score-7-lambda5em3,probe-qwen-score-7-lambda5em2,probe-qwen-score-7-lambda5em1

remaining_length.note: Identical to scripts/cloud/sfs-score-campaign-20260917.json so each probe differs from the canonical qwen-score-7 cell by lambda and by its request budget alone: only the qwen3-0.6b server receives --remaining-length-mode running_all --remaining-length-table qwen3-0.6b.json --remaining-length-quantile 0.5 --remaining-length-conditioning prompt_bin, and the router attaches that table for its missing-prediction fill on that instance only. only the qwen3-0.6b server receives --remaining-length-mode running_all --remaining-length-table qwen3-0.6b.json --remaining-length-quantile 0.5 --remaining-length-conditioning prompt_bin, and the router attaches that table for its missing-prediction fill on that instance only. qwen3-8b and qwen3-32b stay off: reserve-tail-20260916 README sections 4.2/4.3 (8B target component within noise, hindsight replay worse under every candidate; 32B sub-second either way). Ministral stays off: no Ministral paired evidence (reserve-tail-ministral-20260917 is analysis only), the rule is only plumbed for the Qwen family and scripts.cloud.pool refuses it for a Ministral server. Tables were built from the calibration outputs only (zero overlap with the 16,000 evaluation ids); manifest.json records the build paths on the controller.
